set.title: Later financial statements say the Medical Services Commission was established on 1 July 1968 under the Medical Service Act
set.interpretation_notes: A retrospective statement (2002 statements, note 1; the 2004 statements, https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/practitioner-pro/medical-services-plan/bluebook2004.pdf p. 6 note 1, say the same). 1 July 1968 is the Medical Services Plan's operating start under Medicare. The Commission was constituted by the Medical Services Act, 1967, whose s. 3 was brought into force on 24 March 1967 (OIC 964/1967) and whose first members took office that day (OIC 965/1967). Whether a 1968 statute re-constituted the Commission was not checked.

The first sheriff was appointed in 1857. The nine offices are the bailiwicks of the 1972-73 Gazette roster (atlas:primary-evidence-sheriffs-1973); the consolidating instrument and its day are not found. The Police Act of 1974 is not it: the Attorney General said on 6 June 1974 that Bill 91 had nothing to do with the new sheriff service (Hansard, https://api.lims.leg.bc.ca/hdms/file/Debates/30th4th/30p_04s_740606z.htm, p. 3809).
